children: From The Times of India and Stardust to biographies and award-winning films, Mukherjee’s career spans journalism, literature and cinema
Ram Kamal Mukherjee, the journalist, author and filmmaker known for building a career across Indian cinema, literature and storytelling, celebrated his birthday on 13 September.

Mukherjee’s professional journey began in film journalism, where he developed a reputation for going beyond the conventional celebrity narrative to explore the people and stories shaping Indian cinema. Over the years, he worked with publications including The Times of India, The Asian Age, Mid-Day and Anandabazar Patrika, and later served as Editor-in-Chief of Stardust.
His experience in journalism eventually translated into a career as a biographer. At the age of 29, Mukherjee published
Hema Malini: Diva Unveiled

, beginning a body of literary work that chronicled the lives and careers of prominent figures from Hindi cinema. His subsequent biographies explored personalities including Sanjay Dutt and Mithun Chakraborty, combining research with an accessible narrative approach.
Mukherjee also gained experience on the business and production side of entertainment. He served as Vice President at Pritish Nandy Communications and was associated with Zee TV’s finite series
Bin Kuch Kahe
, adding production and content experience to his journalistic background.
His transition from documenting cinema to creating it came with his directorial debut
Cakewalk
, starring Esha Deol. He subsequently worked across projects including
Season’s Greetings
Rickshawala
Broken Frame
Shubho Bijoya
and
Ek Duaa
Social themes have remained a recurring thread across his filmmaking.
Ek Duaa
, which addressed discrimination against the girl child, received a Special Mention at the 69th National Film Awards, marking an important recognition for his work as a filmmaker.
Mukherjee later turned to history and cultural memory with the Bengali period drama
Binodiini: Ekti Natir Upakhyan

, centred on 19th-century theatre pioneer Binodini Dasi. The film brought together his Bengali cultural roots and his longstanding interest in stories of individuals whose contributions have not always received mainstream recognition.
His work across journalism, literature and cinema was further recognised in 2026 with the Rashtra Ratna Sahitya Puraskar.
Mukherjee’s career, spanning multiple forms of storytelling, reflects a continued interest in documenting people, preserving cultural narratives and bringing overlooked stories to wider audiences.
